chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام:
Concerning the urine of riding animals that gets onto the garment, he disliked it.
So I said: “Are not their meats halal (permissible)?” He said: “Yes, but it is not from that which Allah has made for eating.”

key_terms.أَبْوَالِ: urine; here referring to the urine of animals
key_terms.الثَّوْبَ: the garment or clothing affected by impurity
key_terms.جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ لِلْأَكْلِ: that which Allah has designated for eating
key_terms.حَلَالًا: permissible for consumption under the Sacred Law
key_terms.فَكَرِهَهُ: he disliked it; indicating legal disapproval here
key_terms.لُحُومُهَا: their meat; the edible flesh of those animals

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the urine of halal animals if it gets on clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling concerning the urine of riding animals when it reaches one's garment. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes between the permissibility of the animal's meat and the impurity or disapproved status of its urine, clarifying that what Allah has made lawful for eating does not imply the same ruling for all of the animal's bodily substances.
